title: Tallyholden Review 2026: Pros, Cons & Honest Verdict
description: Tallyholden review: the $250 minimum deposit, a name that sounds like accounting, and why regulation and ownership remain unconfirmed.
author: Olivia Bennett
excerpt: Tallyholden sounds like a record-keeping firm, but we could not confirm who runs it or how it is regulated.
content:
Tallyholden combines “tally” (a count or record) with a “-holden” ending, a name that sounds like accounting and old-world holdings. A name is a marketing choice, not a credential, and the details matter far more than the branding.

Strip the branding away and this appears to be another browser-based AI trading platform. The standard pitch applies: a $250 starting deposit, automated or assisted trades, and upbeat talk about returns. The useful question is whether anyone accountable stands behind it.

What Tallyholden Actually Is

Tallyholden follows the usual pattern for this category: a web dashboard, signal-assisted trades, and settings you adjust yourself. Nothing about the mechanics is unusual. What is missing is clear information about who runs it.

What We Could Verify

Our checks did not turn up a confirmed operator, regulator, or operating history for Tallyholden. The $250 minimum deposit matches what most platforms in this category ask, so it says little about whether the service is trustworthy.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Start with the $250 minimum, and nothing more.
  • Use any demo mode before going live.
  • Check the registration or licence number against the actual regulator.
  • Confirm who owns and runs the platform.

Cost Notes

The minimum deposit is $250. Platform trading fees are not independently verified, so confirm the exact fee and spread structure in the current terms before funding. Treat any “no fees” claim with the same caution as any other marketing.

Risks to Keep in Mind

Without a confirmed regulator, you have limited protection if a withdrawal is refused or an account is frozen. Even a legitimate signal platform cannot remove ordinary market losses.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the minimum deposit for Tallyholden?

$250 is the minimum. Consider starting there and no higher.

Is Tallyholden regulated?

We could not independently verify a regulator. Check the registration number yourself.

Does Tallyholden charge platform fees?

Fees are unverified. Check the spreads and any withdrawal charges first.

Does the AI protect me from losses?

No. It reduces effort, not risk. Keep monitoring your open positions.

Where We Land on Tallyholden

Tallyholden has the look of a typical AI trading platform, but little we could confirm sits behind it. Our rating reflects that gap and should be read as a cautious, category-level score.

Keep the first deposit at $250, practise on a demo account where one exists, and treat every return claim as unproven.
